request.spec:
The sheet has claim templates: a name, an amount and a note, saved from a form (TEMPLATE_SAVED
name=<name> amount=<amount> note=<note>; a blank name or an amount the claim form would refuse is
refused with an error on the form; saving a name again replaces that template). Each person's row
has a template select and a button that adds a DRAFT claim with the template's amount and note at
that moment, dated like a claim with no date, by every rule of the claim form (CLAIM_ADDED as the
form writes it). Changing or re-saving the template later does not alter claims made from it.

agent.result_text:
Claim templates are in, and all 4 acceptance tests pass when I run `bin/e2e`.

**Port problem:** my first run failed every test, but not because of the code. My shell has `PORT=3001` set, and 3001 (along with 3002–3004) is already held by other apps, probably other runs going at the same time. So my build never started, and the tests ran against whatever is on that port. I didn't touch those processes and ran on a free port with `PORT=3047 bin/e2e`. If you run `bin/e2e` with the default you may hit the same clash.

**What I added:**
- **Stored data:** a migration `V62__claim_template.sql` adds a `claim_template` table: one row per sheet and name, holding an amount and a note.
- **Server** (new package `net.officefloor.hq.app.template`):
  - **Saving a template:** it is saved under its trimmed name, and saving the same name again replaces it. It writes `TEMPLATE_SAVED … name= amount= note=` to the audit file. A blank name is refused, and so is an amount the claim form wouldn't take on a plain claim (more than two decimals, or below 0.00).
  - **Adding a claim from a template:** the server looks the template up at that moment and passes its amount and note to the existing claim-adding code with no date. That means it follows every claim-form rule: the entry date or today, the closed-period check, late entries, and `CLAIM_ADDED` plus the rollups exactly as the form writes them. Because the amount and note are copied, changing or re-saving the template later doesn't alter claims already made from it.
- **Front end:**
  - A new "Claim templates" section on the main screen with the save form and a list of saved templates.
  - Each person's claim form now has a template select (`claim-template-select`) and an add button (`claim-template-add`). A refusal shows in the existing `claim-form-error`, which clears when you pick another template or press the button again.
